title: Takrur adopts Islam
description: King War Jabi of Takrur converts, making his kingdom on the Senegal River one of the first Muslim states south of the Sahara.

title: Jolof Empire founded
description: By tradition Ndiadiane Ndiaye unites the Wolof states under one ruler.

title: Portuguese reach Cap-Vert
description: Dinis Dias sails past the mouth of the Senegal River and reaches the westernmost point of Africa.

title: Battle of Danki
description: Kayor defeats its Jolof overlord and the empire breaks up into separate Wolof kingdoms.

title: Saint-Louis founded
description: French traders build a fort on an island in the mouth of the Senegal River, the first lasting French settlement in West Africa.

title: French take Gorée
description: A French squadron captures the island from the Dutch, and it remains a French trading post, dealing in slaves among other goods, for most of the next three centuries.

title: British capture Saint-Louis
description: A British expedition takes the French posts in Senegal during the Seven Years' War and holds Saint-Louis until 1783.

title: Imamate of Futa Toro founded
description: Muslim clerics overthrow the Denianke rulers of the middle Senegal valley and set up a state led by an elected almamy.

title: Slavery abolished
description: The French decree of abolition frees the slaves of Saint-Louis and Gorée, whose inhabitants also gain the right to elect a deputy to the French parliament.

title: Faidherbe becomes governor
description: Louis Faidherbe begins the military expansion that turns a few trading posts into a colony reaching far up the Senegal River.

title: Dakar founded
description: The French establish a military post on the mainland opposite Gorée, which grows into the chief port of West Africa.

title: Dakar to Saint-Louis railway opens
description: The first railway in French West Africa crosses Kayor and opens the groundnut-growing interior to export.

title: Death of Lat Dior
description: The ruler of Kayor, who had resisted the railway and French control, is killed in battle and his kingdom is annexed.

title: French West Africa established
description: France groups its West African colonies under a governor-general based in Senegal, moving the seat to Dakar in 1902.

title: Blaise Diagne elected
description: Voters of the Four Communes send the first black African deputy to the French National Assembly.

title: Battle of Dakar
description: British and Free French forces fail in three days to take the port from the Vichy authorities.

title: Thiaroye massacre
description: French troops fire on West African soldiers, former prisoners of war, who are demanding their back pay.

title: Independence in the Mali Federation
description: Senegal and the French Sudan become independent from France as a single federation with its capital at Dakar.

title: Senegal leaves the Mali Federation
description: After a dispute between the leaders of the two territories Senegal declares its own independence, and Léopold Sédar Senghor becomes its first president.

title: Arrest of Mamadou Dia
description: A confrontation between President Senghor and his prime minister ends with Dia's arrest and a strongly presidential constitution.

title: Senghor steps down
description: Léopold Sédar Senghor resigns voluntarily after twenty years as president and hands over to Abdou Diouf.

title: Senegambia Confederation
description: Senegal and the Gambia join in a loose confederation, which is dissolved in 1989.

title: Casamance conflict begins
description: Troops break up a separatist march in the southern region's capital, starting a long low-level insurgency.

title: Abdoulaye Wade elected
description: The opposition leader defeats Abdou Diouf, who concedes, ending forty years of Socialist Party rule by a peaceful vote.

title: Sinking of the Joola
description: An overloaded state ferry from Ziguinchor to Dakar capsizes in a storm and more than 1,800 people die.

title: Macky Sall elected
description: Abdoulaye Wade, seeking a disputed third term, loses the run-off and concedes to his former prime minister.
